title: Nightly TP overload canary + stall/watchdog alerting
author: Sahana Iyer
body: Context: As part of the TP stability initiative we need a nightly signal that exercises multi-GPU tensor-parallel under sustained overload and surfaces stalls before customers do. This PR adds a new scheduled GitHub Actions workflow that runs the TP overload scenarios against the canary environment, publishes artifacts, and alerts when we see watchdog triggers or stall signatures. What this adds: (1) New workflow `.github/workflows/tp-overload-nightly.yml` scheduled nightly (and `workflow_dispatch`) that runs TP overload suites on the canary runner with a hard timeout + per-step timeouts. (2) Scenario config `scenarios/tp_overload_nightly.yaml` that mixes long streams + short prompts, includes cancellation/disconnect patterns, and forces mixed sequence lengths to stress the scheduler. (3) Stall/watchdog detection in the result parser: flags `watchdog_triggered`, `collective_stall_suspected`, `no_forward_progress` based on canary logs + JSON counters emitted by the runtime harness. (4) Alerting: posts a summary to `#eng-sre` and `#eng-runtime` via our existing canary Slack notifier, and emits a `canary.tp_overload` event with the run URL + artifact link. Alerts are only sent on (a) stall/watchdog detected OR (b) failure in 2 consecutive nightly runs to reduce noise from transient infra. (5) Artifacts: uploads full logs + parsed summary JSON; keeps the last 30 days. Operational notes: Workflow uses `concurrency: tp-overload-nightly` to prevent overlapping runs; requires `CANARY_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` + `CANARY_ENV_TOKEN` secrets (already present in repo envs). Default target is `canary-us-east-1` (Dedicated-like pool) with `TP=4` and `TP=8` sub-matrix when capacity is available; if TP=8 capacity is exhausted, the job marks that axis as skipped and does not page. Validation: (a) dry-run against staging with forced `--inject-rank-delay` produced an alert and artifact bundle, (b) normal run for 3 hours produced no alerts and stable latency/throughput within expected bands. Follow-ups: Once runtime PRs for watchdog/quarantine land broadly, we should tighten thresholds and add a weekly longer soak (6h) to increase sensitivity without increasing nightly runtime. Release/rollout: No production changes; this is CI/canary-only.
commits: ci: add nightly tp overload workflow with concurrency + timeouts
scenarios: introduce tp_overload_nightly config (streams + cancels + mixed seq lens)
reporting: parse watchdog/stall signals and gate alerts on consecutive failures
reporting: upload parsed summary.json and link in Slack message
docs: add runbook snippet for interpreting tp overload alerts
conversation:
Rafael Mendes (review): Can we avoid paging on a single flaky run? We’ve had occasional runner hiccups that look like timeouts but aren’t TP-related.
Sahana Iyer (author): Yep. Added a small state file persisted in the artifacts bucket keyed by workflow name that records last run status. We now alert on stall/watchdog immediately (high signal), but for generic failures we require 2 consecutive nights. Also added explicit runner health checks so we fail fast with a different error code.

Sofia Ivanova (review): Scenario mix looks good, but I want to ensure we stress the cancellation path (streaming disconnect) because that’s where the barrier deadlock showed up. Are we guaranteeing cancels under load?
Sahana Iyer (author): Good call. Updated `tp_overload_nightly.yaml` to include a 20% cancellation rate during the long-stream phase and a phase that cancels at deterministic token offsets. Also added a check in the parser for “cancel pending > 60s” which we saw in the deadlock signature.

Marcus Reed (review): What’s the definition of “no_forward_progress”? We should be careful not to flag slow but healthy runs (e.g., when capacity is constrained).
Sahana Iyer (author): Currently: if per-rank progress counter doesn’t advance for 90s while there are in-flight requests, and we also see collective latency p95 > 30s for at least 3 consecutive windows. I made both thresholds configurable in `thresholds.py` and documented how to tune. Also added an explicit “capacity constrained” skip condition if the harness reports admission is blocked and queue depth is near zero.

Allison Grant (review): Please include links to the dashboard/runbook in the Slack message to reduce triage time.
Sahana Iyer (author): Done. Slack payload now includes the run URL, artifact link, and the internal dashboard deep link, plus `docs/canaries/tp-overload.md` for first steps.

Rafael Mendes (review): Any risk this overlaps with other nightly canaries and causes noisy contention in the canary pool?
Sahana Iyer (author): Added `concurrency` to prevent overlap with itself and scheduled it at 03:20 UTC which is outside our heaviest canary windows. Also limiting max parallel jobs to 1 for this workflow.

Rafael Mendes (final): Approved assuming CI is green.
Sofia Ivanova (final): Approved.
Marcus Reed (final): Approved after thresholds config change.

CI: Initial run failed due to missing `CANARY_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` in the `staging` environment; updated workflow to only post Slack for `canary` envs and added a no-op notifier for PR runs. Re-run green.
release_notes: Internal: Adds nightly TP overload perf-canary and Slack alerting on TP watchdog/stall signatures (no customer-facing change).
